rag_questions.question: What is the difference between PERFECT=True and PERFECT=False in A-Maze-ing?
rag_questions.answer: PERFECT=True gives a perfect maze with exactly one path between entry and exit; PERFECT=False (the default) gives a Pac-Man-style board with the corners and center open, at least two routes and no dead-ends.

rag_questions.question: When is the hidden 42 pattern left out of the maze?
rag_questions.answer: When the maze is too small to fit it: under 7 cells tall or 9 cells wide; a console warning is printed instead.

rag_questions.question: What is needed to run the graphical display of A-Maze-ing?
rag_questions.answer: The MiniLibX Python bindings (src/mlx-*.whl) and their native dependencies (X11 on Linux), besides Python 3.10+ and make.

rag_questions.question: Which make rule rebuilds the mazegen wheel?
rag_questions.answer: make package rebuilds mazegen-*.whl from the current source of mazegen/.

rag_questions.question: Which configuration keys are required and which are optional?
rag_questions.answer: WIDTH, HEIGHT, ENTRY, EXIT, OUTPUT_FILE and SEED are required; PERFECT, PLAYABLE, COLOR (default False) and TERMINAL (default True) are optional.

rag_questions.question: What is the maximum maze size allowed?
rag_questions.answer: 40x25 cells (WIDTH/HEIGHT); anything larger is rejected with an error message.

rag_questions.question: Which key shows the next shortest path in the terminal renderer?
rag_questions.answer: n cycles to the next available shortest path, only when PLAYABLE=False (p shows or hides the path).

rag_questions.question: How does the Crazy game mode work?
rag_questions.answer: A time-attack mode: it starts on a perfect 4x4 maze with a 15-second timer; each exit reached grows the maze by one row and column and adds time; when time runs out the level is saved in highscore.txt.

rag_questions.question: Why does the player keep moving in a corridor without pressing keys?
rag_questions.answer: In PLAYABLE mode movement auto-continues in a straight corridor, Pac-Man style; w/a/s/d are only needed at forks.

rag_questions.question: Which keys control the MiniLibX graphical renderer?
rag_questions.answer: w/a/s/d move the player, p shows the animated shortest path, r regenerates, m changes the theme and Esc quits.

rag_questions.question: What is the format of the maze output file?
rag_questions.answer: One hexadecimal digit per cell (bit 0=North, 1=East, 2=South, 3=West, 1 = closed), one row per line, then a blank line, the entry, the exit and a shortest path as N/E/S/W letters.

rag_questions.question: Why was the recursive backtracker chosen to generate the maze?
rag_questions.answer: It always gives a perfect maze (a spanning tree), it is iterative so it cannot overflow the call stack, and its long winding corridors look better and made the 42 and 3x3 rules easier.

rag_questions.question: How is a perfect maze turned into the Pac-Man playable board?
rag_questions.answer: The corners and center get at least two open walls, extra walls are removed to create at least two loops, and dead-ends are opened until none are left, never creating a fully open 3x3 area.

rag_questions.question: Who wrote the maze solver and the graphical renderer of A-Maze-ing?
rag_questions.answer: albrodri: the solver (flood fill and path reconstruction) and the whole MiniLibX renderer; saperez- did the generator and the terminal side.

rag_questions.question: What took more time than expected in the A-Maze-ing project?
rag_questions.answer: The recursive flood fill of the solver (needing a higher recursion limit, fragile on large mazes) and the MiniLibX Python bindings (keycodes, image loading, flicker).

rag_questions.question: What is the difference between grid and maze in mazegen?
rag_questions.answer: grid is list[str] with one hex digit per cell plus a trailing empty string; maze is list[list[int]] that may keep the VISITED bit (16). Both are indexed [y][x].

rag_questions.question: How does mazegen keep a maze reproducible?
rag_questions.answer: Every random choice uses a random.Random(seed) created for that call, never the global random state; the same height, width, seed and perfect give the same maze, and seed=None picks one seed once.

rag_questions.question: What does regenerate do when no seed is given?
rag_questions.answer: The seed defaults to -1, which advances the internal seed by a small random increment; the previous solution is discarded.

rag_questions.question: When does MazeGen.solve raise an error?
rag_questions.answer: If generate() was not called, if entry/exit are outside the maze or equal, or if no path exists between them (e.g. inside a locked 42 cell).

rag_questions.question: How does mazegen find every shortest path?
rag_questions.answer: A breadth-first flood fill from the exit records distances, then a backtrack from the entry follows neighbours whose distance is one less, branching to return all tied shortest paths.

rag_questions.question: Which mazegen modules are internal and how are they imported?
rag_questions.answer: maze_generator_dependences, hexa_dependences and maze_solver_dependences; they are not re-exported (only MazeGen and MazeGenError), so they are imported from their submodule.

rag_questions.question: How can the mazegen package be installed?
rag_questions.answer: From a prebuilt wheel (pip install mazegen-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl), by building a wheel with python -m build, or in editable mode with pip install -e .

rag_questions.question: What coordinate convention does mazegen use for cells?
rag_questions.answer: (x, y) pairs, x the column (< width) and y the row (< height), for entry, exit and solution coordinates.

rag_questions.question: What size, exit and seed does the config.txt shipped with A-Maze-ing use?
rag_questions.answer: WIDTH=15, HEIGHT=15, ENTRY=0,0, EXIT=14,14 and SEED=1234, with PERFECT=False.

rag_questions.question: Who holds the best score in the A-Maze-ing highscore file?
rag_questions.answer: saperez- with 999, followed by albrodri with 998.
